final.memo:
Ligand Pharmaceuticals represents a classic distressed situation where a governance-induced accounting crisis has led the market to abandon a company possessing a legitimate portfolio of pharmaceutical products and intellectual property [D01, D03]. While the market is currently preoccupied with the company’s delisting and ongoing financial restatements for 2002-2004, this volatility masks an underlying asset value that remains intact [D03, D05, D07].

When evaluating the business against industry peers like Amgen, who command healthy EBIT margins near 39%, Ligand’s recent performance is clearly unacceptable [D06]. We value the underlying IP and product portfolio at approximately $650 million, suggesting a normalized value of $14.50 per share once the firm regains its footing and relists [D04, D06]. With $73.8 million in cash providing an absolute floor, the current trading price near $10.14 offers an asymmetric risk/reward profile [D04].

Our plan is simple: we intend to force immediate transparency regarding the restatement timeline and push for an audit committee refresh to restore Nasdaq compliance [D03, D07]. The company’s precarious status creates a natural urgency that management and the current board can no longer ignore [D03]. We expect this governance intervention to occur within two quarters; should our initial demands for accountability go unheeded, we are prepared to escalate our role, including the nomination of a slate of directors at the next annual meeting [D03].

We recognize the risks inherent in the current accounting uncertainty and the potential for hidden liabilities, which is why we are sizing this position at 5% of NAV—a weight appropriate for a distressed event with significant upside [D03, D05]. We will exit this position either when the market re-rates the stock post-relisting or if the restatement process reveals that the core IP is fundamentally impaired. We seek to capture the value that the current management has failed to protect.
